name: Margaret River
label: left
text: Surrounded on three sides by the Indian and Southern oceans, Margaret River's mild, even climate gives elegant, structured Cabernet and some of Australia's most celebrated Chardonnay.

name: Geographe
label: right
text: Just north of Margaret River, Geographe runs from the coast into the hills, with sea breezes tempering warm days for bright Chardonnay and medium-bodied reds.

name: Pemberton
label: bottom
text: Among the tall karri forests of WA's south-west, Pemberton's cooler, wetter climate suits fine Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

name: Great Southern
label: right
text: A large region on WA's south coast with five subregions, from Frankland River to Albany. Known for taut, citrusy Riesling and peppery, cool-climate Shiraz.

name: Swan District
label: right
text: Western Australia's oldest wine region, including the Swan Valley on Perth's doorstep. Hot summers suit generous whites like Chenin Blanc and Verdelho, and rich fortified wines.

name: Clare Valley
label: right
text: Clare's warm days and cold nights give bone-dry, lime-scented Riesling that ages beautifully, along with firm, savoury Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Barossa Valley
label: left
text: Home to some of the world's oldest Shiraz vines, the Barossa makes rich, generous reds full of dark fruit and spice, and old-vine Grenache and Mataro.

name: Eden Valley
label: right
text: Higher and cooler than its Barossa neighbour, Eden Valley is famous for fine, floral Riesling and elegant, perfumed Shiraz.

name: Adelaide Hills
label: right
text: In the Mount Lofty Ranges above Adelaide, altitude keeps things cool: crisp Sauvignon Blanc, fine Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling.

name: McLaren Vale
label: left
text: Between the Mount Lofty Ranges and the sea, McLaren Vale's Mediterranean climate gives ripe, generous Shiraz with a savoury edge, and celebrated old-vine Grenache.

name: Langhorne Creek
label: right
text: Cooled by breezes off Lake Alexandrina, Langhorne Creek makes soft, generous reds, and its grapes find their way into many well-known blends.

name: Riverland
label: left
text: Irrigated by the Murray River, the Riverland is one of Australia's biggest producing regions, and a growing home for Mediterranean and alternative varieties.

name: Coonawarra
label: left
text: A narrow strip of red terra rossa soil over limestone gives Coonawarra its famous Cabernet Sauvignon: blackcurrant, mint and fine, firm tannins.

name: Grampians
label: right
text: Around Great Western, the Grampians has a long history of sparkling wine, including sparkling Shiraz, and makes peppery, medium-bodied still Shiraz.

name: Heathcote
label: left
text: Deep red Cambrian soils, formed more than 500 million years ago, give Heathcote's Shiraz its depth, structure and dark, plummy fruit.

name: Goulburn Valley
label: top
text: Along the Goulburn River, including the Nagambie Lakes subregion, known for structured Shiraz and long-lived Marsanne.

name: Macedon Ranges
label: left
text: One of mainland Australia's coolest wine regions, just north-west of Melbourne. Ideal for fine sparkling, taut Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

name: Geelong
label: left
text: Around Port Phillip and the Bellarine Peninsula, Geelong's cool, windy climate makes intense Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and spicy Shiraz.

name: Yarra Valley
label: right
text: Victoria's first wine region, an hour from Melbourne. Elegant Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, fine sparkling, and medium-bodied Cabernet and Shiraz.

name: Mornington Peninsula
label: bottom
text: Surrounded by sea on three sides, the Peninsula's cool maritime climate is made for Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and textural Pinot Gris.

name: Gippsland
label: right
text: A large, sparsely planted region east of Melbourne, with small producers making characterful Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

name: King Valley
label: right
text: Settled by Italian families, the King Valley is the home of Australian Prosecco and a hub for Italian varieties like Pinot Grigio, Sangiovese and Nebbiolo.

name: Beechworth
label: right
text: A small, high region in north-east Victoria with a big reputation for powerful, complex Chardonnay and Shiraz.

name: Rutherglen
label: left
text: Famous for its world-class fortified Muscat and Topaque, aged for decades, and big, inky reds from Durif and Shiraz.

name: Riverina
label: right
text: Around Griffith, irrigated vineyards make a large share of Australia's everyday wine, and the region is famous for luscious botrytis Semillon dessert wine.

name: Tumbarumba
label: left
text: In the foothills of the Snowy Mountains, Tumbarumba's high, cool vineyards give fine Chardonnay and base wine for top sparkling.

name: Canberra District
label: right
text: Spanning the ACT and southern NSW, the Canberra District is known for fragrant Shiraz, often co-fermented with a little Viognier, and fine Riesling.

name: Hilltops
label: left
text: Around Young, Hilltops' elevated vineyards and warm days give deeply coloured, full-flavoured Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Orange
label: left
text: Defined by altitude, with vineyards above 600 metres on the slopes of Mount Canobolas. Crisp whites, Pinot Noir and cool-climate Shiraz.

name: Mudgee
label: right
text: On the western slopes of the Great Dividing Range, Mudgee makes generous, full-bodied reds and rich Chardonnay.

name: Hunter Valley
label: left
text: One of Australia's oldest wine regions. Hunter Semillon is picked early, light in alcohol and ages for decades; Hunter Shiraz is medium-bodied and earthy.

name: Granite Belt
label: right
text: Queensland's high-country wine region, with vineyards at altitude on granite soils, and a reputation for alternative 'Strange Bird' varieties.

name: Tasmania
label: right
text: Australia's coolest wine state, from the Tamar Valley in the north to the Coal River and Huon valleys in the south. World-class sparkling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Riesling.

name: Perth Hills
label: right
text: In the Darling Range east of Perth, where altitude takes the edge off the heat. Small producers make Shiraz, Cabernet and Chardonnay.

name: Peel
label: left
text: A small region south of Perth around Mandurah and the Peel Inlet, with warm weather suited to Shiraz and Chenin Blanc.

name: Blackwood Valley
label: right
text: Inland from Margaret River around Bridgetown and Boyup Brook, with warm days and cool nights for Shiraz, Cabernet and Chardonnay.

name: Manjimup
label: right
text: Among the karri and jarrah forests of the south-west, Manjimup's cool climate suits Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Merlot.

name: Southern Flinders Ranges
label: right
text: North of the Clare Valley in the foothills of the Flinders Ranges, making full-flavoured Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Adelaide Plains
label: left
text: On the flat, warm plains north of Adelaide, making ripe, generous reds and whites.

name: Kangaroo Island
label: left
text: Surrounded by the Southern Ocean, the island's maritime climate gives fresh, elegant wines from a small number of producers.

name: Southern Fleurieu
label: left
text: South of McLaren Vale, cooled by breezes from two coastlines, making fresh whites and elegant Shiraz.

name: Currency Creek
label: right
text: Near Goolwa and the mouth of the Murray, with sea and lake breezes moderating the warmth.

name: Padthaway
label: left
text: On the Limestone Coast, long a source of quality Chardonnay and Shiraz for both blends and estate wines.

name: Mount Benson
label: left
text: Close to the Southern Ocean near Kingston SE, with cool sea breezes for crisp whites and medium-bodied reds.

name: Robe
label: left
text: A small coastal region around the fishing town of Robe, with a cool, maritime climate.

name: Wrattonbully
label: right
text: Just north of Coonawarra, with similar terra rossa soils over limestone, known for Cabernet and Shiraz.

name: Mount Gambier
label: right
text: One of South Australia's coolest regions, near the Victorian border, suited to Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc.

name: South Burnett
label: right
text: Queensland's other wine region, around Kingaroy, with warm summers and a mix of reds and whites.

name: New England Australia
label: right
text: On the Northern Tablelands, where high vineyards give cool-climate whites and reds.

name: Hastings River
label: right
text: On the subtropical mid-north coast around Port Macquarie, where humidity favours hardy varieties like Chambourcin.

name: Cowra
label: left
text: Best known for generous, fruit-forward Chardonnay from warm, sunny vineyards.

name: Southern Highlands
label: right
text: In the elevated country south-west of Sydney, cool and relatively wet, suited to Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and aromatic whites.

name: Shoalhaven Coast
label: right
text: On the NSW South Coast around Nowra and Berry, with warm, humid summers and a mix of varieties including Chambourcin.

name: Gundagai
label: left
text: Between the Riverina and the high country, making full-bodied Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Perricoota
label: right
text: On the NSW side of the Murray River near Moama, a warm region making generous reds and whites.

name: Murray Darling
label: right
text: Straddling the Victoria–NSW border around Mildura, one of Australia's biggest producing regions, irrigated by the Murray.

name: Swan Hill
label: left
text: Along the Murray around Swan Hill, straddling Victoria and NSW, with warm, irrigated vineyards.

name: Glenrowan
label: left
text: Next to Rutherglen in north-east Victoria, known for robust reds and fortified wines.

name: Alpine Valleys
label: right
text: Valleys at the foot of the Victorian Alps around Myrtleford and Bright, known for Italian and alternative varieties.

name: Strathbogie Ranges
label: right
text: Granite hills between Nagambie and the high country, cool and elevated, making Riesling, Shiraz and sparkling base.

name: Upper Goulburn
label: right
text: Around Mansfield and Lake Eildon in the foothills of the Alps, making cool-climate whites and reds.

name: Bendigo
label: left
text: Historic gold-rush country, where warm days make rich Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Pyrenees
label: left
text: Around Avoca and Moonambel in western Victoria, known for robust Shiraz and Cabernet.

name: Sunbury
label: bottom
text: Just north-west of Melbourne, cool and windy, known for elegant Shiraz and Chardonnay.

name: Henty
label: right
text: In Victoria's far south-west, one of mainland Australia's coolest wine regions, known for fine Riesling, Pinot Noir and sparkling.
